about: Interaction and content rules with stable IDs. The styleguide renders this file; scripts/styleguide-check.mjs verifies every owner and evidence path exists. Change a rule here, in the owning code, and in its test together.

groups.title: Shared listening and the Discord bot
Finding and hearing music before it is yours

rules.title: A control that cannot act is not drawn
rules.contract: No button that looks live and does nothing, no toggle whose state is decoration. If an action is impossible in this context the control is omitted or replaced by an explained state.
rules.example: The equalizer window ships without traffic lights: three circles that close nothing would be decoration.

rules.title: An unavailable capability says so where the choice is made
rules.contract: Not in a tooltip, not in a log, not by disappearing. The control stays visible and, when chosen, reports the reason instead of acting.
rules.example: The Shared segment of the mode switch stays visible with no hub paired and reports why when pressed.

evidence.name: reports the reason instead of switching when a mode is unavailable
the radio transport: Previous and Next read as unavailable, Play does not, and they say why

rules.title: Say what the code does, not what the feature is called
rules.contract: Labels describe the implemented behaviour. When a label and the DSP (or the network, or the provider) disagree, the label changes.
rules.example: Solfeggio presets are described as filters with no claimed physical effect; retuning states that the fallback changes tempo.

evidence.name: the companion, the container and backup
a link the helper will not fetch from is refused, with the reason

rules.title: A disabled control is still legible about why
rules.contract: Greyed, not gone. The reason is part of the accessible name, not only a tooltip.
rules.example: “500 Hz band, not used by 528 Hz (MI)”.

evidence.name: the companion, the container and backup

rules.title: One tab stop per group; arrows move inside it
rules.contract: Source lists, the section strip, the mode switch, tab strips, tables and menus use a roving tabIndex. Home/End jump, Enter activates, type-ahead selects. Focus travels with the selection.

evidence.name: @a11y the tab strip is navigable with the keyboard alone
has one tab stop, moves with arrows, Home/End, selects with Enter and supports type-ahead
uses a roving tabindex, arrow navigation, Space selection and Enter activation
has one tab stop, moves with arrows and Home/End, chooses with Enter, and answers type-ahead

rules.title: Focus is always visible
rules.contract: Every focusable element shows --aqua-focus-shadow or a 2px --np-accent outline at 2px offset, including when the ring is drawn on an ancestor via :focus-within.

evidence.name: @a11y focus is visible wherever it lands

rules.title: Every action is reachable with the keyboard alone
rules.contract: Every section and every transport control can be reached and operated without a pointer. Space toggles playback without scrolling the page.

evidence.name: @a11y the transport is reachable and named from the keyboard alone
space toggles playback and does not scroll the page
@a11y the tab strip is navigable with the keyboard alone

rules.title: Nothing interactive is under 44px on a coarse pointer
rules.contract: Under (pointer: coarse) controls grow; where the visual cannot grow, a transparent ::after takes the taps. Desktop keeps its 18px rows. Hit targets are never shrunk to match a visual; --aqua-hit is 32px on desktop, 44px on touch.

evidence.name: nothing overflows, no text under 12px, no target under 44px
the desktop keeps the design it was drawn with
every screen of every product fits at every size

rules.title: No text under 12px on touch; field text is 16px
rules.contract: The touch layer steps the scale up (15/14/13/12/11px). A field's text is 16px because iOS zooms the page when a smaller field takes focus.

evidence.name: settings, where every panel of explanatory text lives

rules.title: Every data view answers empty, loading and error
rules.contract: A view that fetches renders LoadingState while waiting, ErrorState with a retry when it fails, and an EmptyState that says what to do next. Blank panes are defects.

evidence.name: before any play: nothing recorded, and no generated source on offer
opens with no music, says so, and raises no errors

rules.title: Motion confirms; reduced motion is a contract
rules.contract: Nothing animates that a person did not just cause. Under prefers-reduced-motion the live dot stops, marquees hold their ellipsis, sheets fade without travel, and the 3D stage stops drifting. New animations read --aqua-anim-state or --aqua-sheet-travel.

evidence.name: @a11y respects reduced motion: nothing loops that a person did not start

rules.title: Progress says what is happening in words
rules.contract: Progress bars carry a name and a value; an indeterminate bar is aria-busy and has text. Live regions are polite and carry one sentence.

evidence.name: progress has a name and value; indeterminate is busy with text

rules.title: Downloaders set themselves up and say how far along they are
rules.contract: yt-dlp, spotDL and (on Windows) FFmpeg are set up without a prompt, in the background, into the app's own tools folder, and only after the file matches the SHA-256 its project published for that release. Each downloader row reads Setting up… with a named progress bar, Ready (adding "Set up automatically" when the app installed it), or Couldn’t set up: <reason> beside a Try Again button; the manual install advice appears only when the tool cannot be set up on this machine. Only failed or unsupported tools count as missing — in the companion's Settings badge and on the player's Connections card, where a tool on its way reads "setting up". Where FFmpeg's absence explains an empty Tempo column, the Library says whether it is on its way or could not be set up.
rules.example: Settings ▸ Downloaders: “ffmpeg — Setting up… 42%” with a progress bar; “spotdl — Couldn’t set up: GitHub did not answer (503).” and Try Again. Music: “Setting up ffmpeg — tempos appear once it finishes.”

evidence.name: Settings shows setting up with progress, ready and set up automatically, and a failure with Try Again
Settings keeps the install advice for a tool this PC cannot set up
the Library says tempos are on their way while ffmpeg is being set up
the Library points to Settings when ffmpeg could not be set up, and says nothing once it is ready
sets missing downloaders up by itself, reports how that went, and tries again on request
refuses bytes that do not match the published digest, and leaves nothing behind
records a failure and waits six hours before trying again, unless told to try now

rules.title: Roles are true and colour is never the only signal
rules.contract: A rail that cannot be dragged is role=img, not a slider that refuses changes. Icon buttons have names. The playing row has a glyph as well as a tint; status dots carry text.

evidence.name: live scrubber is not a slider and shows the LIVE marker
icon buttons require names; menu affordance sets aria-haspopup

rules.title: A download is a link
rules.contract: Downloads and destinations in another tab use ButtonLink (an <a> wearing the button face), never a <button> that assigns location.

evidence.name: after real plays: the page counts them, and export and import round-trip them

rules.title: Destructive actions are worded plainly and confirmed
rules.contract: The button names the consequence (“Forget this hub”, “Remove folder”), sits apart from the default action, and the hub and companion ask before doing it.

evidence.title: marks the destructive item, separates it, and never puts it first

evidence.note: Each new destructive action is reviewed for wording and confirmation.

rules.title: The bootstrap password must be replaced before anything else
rules.contract: admin/admin signs in once, straight into Change password. Every setup-gated screen refuses until then, and the hub stays on loopback outside a container.

evidence.name: refuses every setup-gated route until the password is changed
@a11y the sign-in screen has no detectable violations

rules.title: Pairing is confirmed by comparing a fingerprint
rules.contract: A device receives a scoped credential only after the administrator confirms the fingerprint shown on both screens. Codes are never listed again after they are issued.

evidence.name: issues a scoped credential only after the fingerprint is confirmed

rules.title: Privacy claims are stated where they can be checked
rules.contract: Copy that says nothing is uploaded, copied or moved must be true of the code path beside it, and the player loads nothing from outside its own origin.

evidence.name: fetching a link puts a real track in the library, and it plays from this device
loads nothing from outside its own origin, including three.js

rules.title: The shared queue rejects stale commands and says so
rules.contract: Every queue command carries the revision it was based on. A stale command is refused with the current revision, never applied over someone else's change.

rules.title: Slash and prefix commands behave identically
rules.contract: Both transports run through one CommandService and render the same templates; the only difference is how the reply is delivered.

evidence.name: produces identical outcomes for every command

rules.title: Refusals are private and say what was needed
rules.contract: permissionDenied, noResults, unavailableSource, emptyQueue, wrongChannel and error replies are ephemeral and name the reason or the channel to use.

evidence.name: applies the same permission decision on both transports

rules.title: The bot never goes silent without a reason
rules.contract: A track the bot cannot play is skipped with the reason recorded; a failed decode advances as an error; the admin panel shows the voice state and last error.

evidence.name: skips a track it cannot play instead of going silent
shows the worker’s live status in the hub

rules.title: Empty states say what to do next
rules.contract: Title names the situation in a few plain words (“Nothing queued”); text gives the next action or the reason. No apologies, no exclamation marks.
rules.example: “Nothing queued — Play something from your library and it will appear here.”

rules.title: Errors explain the problem and the way out
rules.contract: Name what failed in the person's terms and what fixes it (“Add a bot token first (Admin → Discord → Token)”). Never show a stack trace or an internal identifier; a 500 carries a correlation id instead.

rules.title: One product name, set in one place
rules.contract: “Now Playing” and the product names come from BRANDING in TypeScript. Native resources that cannot import it (Android strings.xml, the SVG icons' aria-labels, the Electron builder config) repeat it and must be changed together.

evidence.title: VOICE-003: the product name is set once

rules.title: One component, one reference
rules.contract: Every component reconstructs one named Apple release (iPod classic, iTunes 10, OS X 10.6, iOS 5…) and is sampled from it, not averaged. Eras mix across components, never inside one. The reference is written beside the component's tokens.
rules.example: The contextual menu is OS X 10.6 (opaque, 5px radius, 20px rows, 13px text); the action sheet that replaces it on touch is iOS 5/6.

evidence.name: era metrics, keyboard nav intact, escape closes, menu action still fires
dark menu opaque

rules.title: Unavailable is shown and explained, never hidden
rules.contract: A control that cannot act in this context stays visible and focusable, is marked aria-disabled, looks disabled, and says why when pressed or hovered. It is not removed and it does not silently do nothing.
rules.example: On a station, previous and next are greyed, titled 'Not available for radio', and pressing them says 'Pick another station from the list'.

evidence.name: the radio transport: Previous and Next read as unavailable, Play does not, and they say why
the tab opens on stations, not on a menu, and the panel is the song list’s own rules
avatar gradient not black; the transport at rest is a slider with every key reachable

rules.title: Measured, not assumed
rules.contract: Numbers shown to the listener come from what actually happened. A track's seconds come from the transport's own clock (a seek is not a listen); stream time is measured from playing to pause/end; anything under five seconds is not a session; a film or song counts as finished only when it played to its end. No invented history, no sample figures — with one labelled exception: Statistics shows a generated demo year while this player has recorded nothing, and says so in the Data menu, the source line and Your data (NPD-023).
rules.example: Statistics opens on this player's own history once anything has played; before that, on a demo year that says it is one.

evidence.name: opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation
it is a page at both widths, and a section has its own address
a track’s seconds are measured, not assumed

rules.title: Values live in tokens, once
rules.contract: Colour, gradient and metric values are CSS custom properties on :root. Components read variables. The dark list is written twice (Auto and forced Dark) and the two copies must be identical.

evidence.note: Carried from airwave-np; its test did not survive the port as a separate assertion. Checked in review against the shell.

rules.title: Menus are opaque
rules.contract: Menus, sheets and popovers of this period had no vibrancy. Their backgrounds are opaque in both themes; only the iOS HUD is translucent.

evidence.name: dark menu opaque

rules.title: Selection is a gradient, not a flat fill
rules.contract: Selected rows and highlighted menu items use the era's two-stop vertical gradient with white text: iTunes 10 blue in lists (--lib-sel-*), Aqua blue in menus (--ctx-hi-*), iPod blue on the iPod screen (--ipod-sel-*).

evidence.note: Carried from airwave-np; its test did not survive the port as a separate assertion. Checked in review against the shell.

rules.title: A live feed says LIVE where the time would be
rules.contract: On Live TV the video controller replaces the elapsed/duration readout with a red LIVE badge, from the moment the tab opens (not only after a channel plays). The badge is centred on the progress rail horizontally in its box and vertically on the rail's centre line at every width.

evidence.name: the Live TV tab is live before a channel is chosen, and a channel does not follow you on to TV
: the LIVE readout sits right, idle and playing
LIVE on the video bar: the tab is live on arrival and a channel keeps it so

rules.title: The progress of a broadcast does not move and cannot be seeked
rules.contract: During a live feed the scrubber is an image (role=img, no range ARIA), the channel loops so LIVE stays true, and pressing it explains instead of seeking.

evidence.name: LIVE on the video bar: the tab is live on arrival and a channel keeps it so
24px optical offset preserved; sort headers are buttons and sorting works; page has h1
avatar gradient not black; the transport at rest is a slider with every key reachable

rules.title: One source sounds at a time
rules.contract: Starting a station stops the video; starting a channel or film stops the station. A film does not follow the listener onto the Live TV or TV tab.

evidence.name: one thing at a time: a channel stops the station, and tuning back stops the channel
the Live TV tab is live before a channel is chosen, and a channel does not follow you on to TV

rules.title: The volume control owns every sound
rules.contract: The volume slider drives the station and the video as well as music; Home is silence and mutes, End is full, the level survives a change of station and a reload.

evidence.name: volume reaches the stream: the slider, Home and End, and a new station keeps the level
the level is remembered across a reload

rules.title: Video starts at the highest quality
rules.contract: A channel, episode or film opens on its highest available rendition; the quality menu lets the viewer step down.

evidence.name: Live TV: the guide replaces the song list, the video player takes the top, and a channel plays

rules.title: The equalizer never silences what it cannot process
rules.contract: Audio is routed through the equalizer only when the browser allows processing it (same-origin, blob:, data:, or the companion). Cross-origin streams play unequalized, and the pane says so.

evidence.name: opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation

rules.title: Right-click opens the item's commands; keys work inside
rules.contract: Right-clicking a song, station, channel, series or film opens an OS X contextual menu at the pointer with the commands for that kind of item. Arrow keys move, Return chooses, Escape closes and returns focus. Scrolling the page after opening does not close it instantly.

evidence.name: era metrics, keyboard nav intact, escape closes, menu action still fires
the song menu is untouched
Radio: a station is played, kept or filed; a new playlist holds it and can be emptied

rules.title: On touch, a long press raises an action sheet
rules.contract: Touch devices get the same commands as an iOS action sheet from a long press, with Cancel last.

evidence.name: long press raises action sheet, listing all commands + playlists + cancel, and its action fires

rules.title: Confirmation is a HUD, not a dialog
rules.contract: A command that completes (added to a playlist, removed) confirms with a brief HUD naming what happened. Dialogs are only for commands that need more input.

evidence.name: era metrics, keyboard nav intact, escape closes, menu action still fires
long press raises action sheet, listing all commands + playlists + cancel, and its action fires

rules.title: Every tab has playlists, behind the library button
rules.contract: Music, Radio, Live TV, TV and Movies each keep their own playlists. They are reached from the library (menu) button on the left of the scope bar, and filled from the item's contextual menu. They persist across reloads.

evidence.name: Radio: a station is played, kept or filed; a new playlist holds it and can be emptied
the playlist is still there after a reload

rules.title: Sorting is a button
rules.contract: Sortable column headers contain buttons and expose aria-sort; the sorted column tints blue (iTunes 10). A set order (a playlist) shows no arrow until a column sort overrides it.

evidence.name: 24px optical offset preserved; sort headers are buttons and sorting works; page has h1
no column may show a sort arrow while the rows are in set order

rules.title: The header search belongs to Music
rules.contract: The status bar's search pill searches songs and takes pasted song links, so it is shown only on Music. Other tabs search with the list's own field.

evidence.name: the header field is up on Music and gone on the other tabs, which keep their own field

rules.title: The profile button opens Settings
rules.contract: The avatar at the right of the status bar opens Settings as its own page (#settings), not a pop-up.

evidence.name: opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation

rules.title: Two idioms: iPhone OS on phones, a toolbar on desktops
rules.contract: Below 720px Settings is an iPhone OS drill-down: an index of 44px rows, a back button that names where it returns to. From 720px it is a preferences window with a toolbar of five panes. The browser Back button walks the same history.

evidence.name: media playlists live behind the library button
opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation

rules.title: A preference applies when it is changed
rules.contract: No Save and no Apply. Theme, motion, artwork, defaults, group mode and every algorithm setting apply immediately and persist (player:prefs). Revert, in the footer, restores everything to how it was when Settings opened (NPD-016).

evidence.name: opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation
player preferences, the equalizer and group mode; the equalizer survives a reload
Revert puts back the weight, the algorithm, and removes the copy

rules.title: The algorithm is editable and cannot be made invalid
rules.contract: Every recommendation setting has a control. Rules the engine enforces (weights summing to 100, ranges) are checked as the user edits and offered a fix, never silently clamped.

evidence.name: opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation

rules.title: One hue for amounts, named hues for genres, and every chart as numbers
rules.contract: Amounts use one hue (--viz-1) with a single-hue ramp for the skyline (--viz-sky-0 → --viz-1 → --viz-peak). Genres use seven token hues (--viz-g1…g7, --viz-g0 for the rest), lifted in dark, and a genre's colour never appears without its name beside it. Every chart has its value written beside it or a table under it, and the 3D views are backed by the same numbers in 2D.

evidence.name: before any play: nothing recorded, and no generated source on offer

rules.title: The video controller fits the player, not the window
rules.contract: Controller-bar content responds to the player's width (container queries): elapsed only under 560px, download and touch volume hidden, More hidden under 358px; the scrubber keeps at least 60px. Checked at 18 device sizes.

evidence.name: : the LIVE readout sits right, idle and playing
px LIVE is centred in its box, clear of its neighbours, and the scrubber keeps room

rules.title: Picture and controls fit under the status bar
rules.contract: On short screens (landscape phones, short laptops) the video player is capped so it and its controls fit below the status bar without scrolling.

evidence.name: : the LIVE readout sits right, idle and playing

rules.title: Every control is reachable and named
rules.contract: Icon-only controls carry accessible names; groups of choices are radiogroups moved with arrow keys; scrolling regions are focusable; headings give the page an outline (one h1).

evidence.name: 24px optical offset preserved; sort headers are buttons and sorting works; page has h1
opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation

rules.title: Motion stops when asked
rules.contract: With the OS reduced-motion setting, or Preferences > Reduce animation, pulses, barber poles, spinners and transitions stop.

evidence.name: opening: Settings is a page with its own address, and the toolbar is the navigation

rules.title: Text meets 4.5:1; exceptions are recorded
rules.contract: Text/background pairs listed in design/foundations.json meet WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 marks) in both themes. Period colours that fall short are recorded as decisions, never added silently.

evidence.note: Carried from airwave-np; its test did not survive the port as a separate assertion. Checked in review against the shell.

rules.title: Commands are Title Case; an ellipsis means a dialog follows
rules.contract: Menu commands use Title Case verbs ('Go to Album', 'Add to Playlist'). An ellipsis marks exactly the commands that open a dialog for more input ('New Playlist…', 'Change Artist…').

evidence.name: six commands in three groups, and an ellipsis marks exactly the dialog commands

rules.title: The verb matches the thing
rules.contract: A song or film is Played, a channel is Watched, a series is Opened. Commands that make no sense for a kind of item are absent from its menu, not disabled.

evidence.name: Live TV: a channel is watched, not played, and its playlist still reads as a guide
Radio: a station is played, kept or filed; a new playlist holds it and can be emptied
the song menu is untouched

rules.title: Explanations are one plain sentence with a way forward
rules.contract: When something cannot happen, say what to do instead in one sentence, without apology or error codes: 'Pick another station from the list', 'Couldn’t reach search — open it on a platform instead:'.

evidence.note: Carried from airwave-np; its test did not survive the port as a separate assertion. Checked in review against the shell.

rules.title: Every figure is set against the period before
rules.contract: For 7, 30, 90 days and the year, each tile compares with the period of the same length just before it, with ▲/▼, the figure, and colour for good or bad news (more skips is up and bad). All time has no period before and shows no comparison. Heard-to-the-end and skips count only plays the transport timed (NPD-018).

evidence.name: statistics against the period before, and the recommendation funnel

rules.title: Recommendations are counted from the shelf's own record
rules.contract: What Discover shows is logged once per song per day; a play started there is a recommendation taken. The funnel reads recommended → started → heard to the end → replayed → added or favourited from those logs, never from estimates.

evidence.name: the shelf records what it shows, and plays from it count
statistics against the period before, and the recommendation funnel

rules.title: The statistics page works without its 3D views
rules.contract: Statistics loads three.js from the page's import map the first time it opens. If that fails or takes more than eight seconds, each 3D well says it couldn't load and the page carries on; every 3D view has the same numbers in 2D or in a table. A theme change repaints the wells, scenes and labels from the tokens.

evidence.name: before any play: nothing recorded, and no generated source on offer
the wells say so, the tables stay

rules.title: Built-in algorithms never change
rules.contract: Airwave default, Late night and Crate digger are read-only. The first change to one makes a named copy, selects it and says so; built-ins cannot be renamed or deleted. Delete asks twice.

evidence.name: built-ins, copies, rename, duplicate, delete, export, import, and a reload

rules.title: Algorithms move as files, and imports say what they read
rules.contract: Export writes one algorithm (or all of yours) as an airwave-algorithm JSON file; Import takes those or a bare engine config, reads only keys the engine knows with values of the right type, and reports how many settings it read and how many it ignored.

evidence.name: the shelf records what it shows, and plays from it count
built-ins, copies, rename, duplicate, delete, export, import, and a reload

rules.title: Settings controls are Mac OS X controls, drawn over native elements
rules.contract: Push buttons, pop-ups and checkboxes in Settings wear Mac OS X drawings: Snow Leopard (10.6) push buttons — a matte, brushed-metal pill with a graphite hairline, blue when pressed — and 10.4 Aqua pop-ups (white body, blue arrow segment) and gel checkboxes that AquaArt draws from sampled colour profiles and publishes as custom properties. The elements stay native button, select and checkbox, so keyboard, forms and screen readers are unchanged. 22px on desktop, 30px on touch; the drawings and their black labels are the same in both themes (NPD-021).

evidence.name: buttons, pop-ups and checkboxes wear the Aqua drawings and still work
the 30px drawings on a phone

rules.title: Connections show what answered and what goes where
rules.contract: Sources ▸ Connections tests the Windows companion app (GET /helper/v1/health; an empty address scans 127.0.0.1:17342–17345) and the Docker container (GET /healthz, /readyz, /api/v1/hub; port 4546), using the AudioWave repo's own endpoints; and Stream from a PC pairs with the companion's AWSP sidecar by its ticket and six-digit code (docs/AWSP.md §2), then shows the PC's name, the connection type (relay-carried in a browser) and how many of its tracks joined the library, with the same lights. Each test shows what came back — version, downloaders, allowed sites, readiness checks, fingerprint, encryption — with a green, amber or red light; every request goes in the connection log with its status and time; and the What's passed table lists each setting, where it goes, and 'Ready' only once that destination has answered.

evidence.name: the companion, the container and backup
pairs, plays relay-carried, is bit-identical, seeks by range, and resumes across a relay restart

rules.title: Backups say what they need before they run
rules.contract: Sources ▸ Backup chooses what to copy (Music, TV, Movies; playlists, EQ presets and settings) and where (the Docker container, the Windows companion app, or both), and how often. Media moves between the companion app and the container, so it needs both to have answered a test and its folder to be set; settings need only their destination. Back Up Now stays disabled and says which of those is missing; once it runs, the request is written to the connection log and What's passed lists a backup row per destination.

evidence.name: the companion, the container and backup

rules.title: Profiles live on the container, and names are unique there
rules.contract: Once the player is paired with the Docker container (the hub's own /pairing/claim, /status and /complete, confirmed by fingerprint), Settings gains a Profile tab: a username, a picture cropped to 256 × 256, and playlists shared as CSV (title, artist, album, seconds), all saved to the container and never kept in the browser. A username someone else has — compared without case — is caught as you type and refused on save. Search lists people on the container above songs; a profile opens in a sheet with their picture, name and shared playlists, and a song you also have can be played from it. Your picture takes the jewel case's place on the Music page. Until the container has the profile routes, the tab says so.

evidence.name: pair, edit the profile on the container, find someone, open their profile

rules.title: One default volume for every source
rules.contract: Settings ▸ Equalizer ▸ Default volume sets the level Airwave opens at — where you left it, or a fixed default — and Set Volume Now moves the bar's volume to it. Music, radio, Live TV, TV and films all start at and follow that one volume.

evidence.name: the default volume: Set Volume Now, then each start mode across a reload

rules.title: Drag a box to pick several songs
rules.contract: On a pointer, pressing on a song row's empty space and dragging draws a rubber band; every row it touches is selected. Cmd/Ctrl-click adds or removes one song, Shift-click takes the range, Cmd/Ctrl-A takes the list, Escape clears. Picking is never playing: the click that ends a drag, and a modified click, start nothing. A plain click goes back to one song and plays it.

evidence.name: dragging draws a selection box, and the menu for several acts on all of them

rules.title: One menu for several songs
rules.contract: Right-clicking inside a selection of several songs opens the contextual menu for all of them: its heading says how many, and each command names the count it will act on — Download N Songs (or Remove N Downloads when all are saved), Add N Songs to Group Queue, Add to Playlist ▸ (ticked only when the playlist holds every one), New Playlist from N Songs…, Deselect All. The selection survives the repaint a command causes.

evidence.name: dragging draws a selection box, and the menu for several acts on all of them

rules.title: A mini player while Settings is open; leaving video stops it
rules.contract: When Music or Radio is the tab and Settings covers the player, the header's search pill becomes a mini player: title and artist, time and duration, play/pause and skip, driving the real transport. Leaving a video tab — for Settings or another tab — pauses a film or episode, and disconnects Live TV (the stream is closed, not just muted).

evidence.name: with Settings open, the header shows a mini player that drives the real transport
video tabs: Settings from Live TV shows no mini player and disconnects; Music pauses a channel

rules.title: A backup says how big it is and whether it fits
rules.contract: Settings ▸ Sources ▸ Backup shows the expected size, part by part, and each destination's free space as a bar (in use · this backup · free after it). Figures the player can't measure itself come from the companion app and the container; until they answer, the row names which figure is waiting and who measures it. Back Up Now is unavailable when the backup doesn't fit. Algorithms can be backed up like the rest. Sizes are decimal (1 GB = 10⁹ bytes).

evidence.name: the companion, the container and backup

rules.title: A listing can be heard before it is added
rules.contract: In the header search popover, a result with a clip plays it on a click of its artwork tile — the whole clip, up to 30 seconds, with a countdown ring and a fade at the tail — and resting a fine pointer on the row for five seconds arms the same play with a visible fill in the selection blue. Leaving the row, a key, a scroll or another row cancels the hold; touch and reduced motion never arm; the click always works. The main track pauses for the audition and resumes after it. A row with no clip keeps its tile and says why on hover instead of dressing as a button. rules.title: Groups and invites live on the Profile tab
rules.contract: Settings ▸ Profile lists your groups on the container with their member count and your role, makes a new one (you own it), and — for an owner or admin whose player was paired with the “Manage groups” permission — makes an invite link that works once and expires after the time chosen. Without that permission no invite link is offered, because the container would refuse it, and the message names the missing permission rather than blaming the role. Invites you have received wait there until you join or decline; ones you have sent show who they were for and when they expire. A code the container can't withdraw is never shown as withdrawn.

rules.title: An invite link opens an invite page
rules.contract: Opening an invite link shows a page naming the group, who sent it, the container, the role and when it expires, with Join Group and Decline (Not Now keeps it waiting). What the link says is labelled as the link's until the container confirms it. An unpaired player, or one paired with another container, is asked to pair first and offered Connections. The code is taken out of the address bar as soon as it has been read.
